change_summary: PLOS ONE issued an Expression of Concern about this article. Fig. 7 does not correspond to its legend or the Results text, and does not report data for an LSD1 siRNA experiment. The stored paper reports that LSD1 siRNA reduced migration in H460 cells. The notice also notes a possible discontinuity in the Fig. 4 LSD1 panel and too little control detail to replicate the transfection experiments. Similarities with other groups' work call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results, and the authors did not respond.
evaluation: Your Section 3 cites [12] for the H460 scratch-assay result that LSD1 siRNA reduced migration, and treats it as the clearest indication that LSD1 drives migration. The notice says Fig. 7 does not report data for an LSD1 siRNA experiment, so that result statement is not supported, which touches the evidence your central hypothesis leans on. Your Background section cites [12] for higher LSD1 in lung cancer tissue than in normal lung in 80 patients. The notice says similarities with other groups' work call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results, but it names no specific problem with the tissue data, so that use is uncertain. Overall the impact is medium, driven by the Section 3 rationale.
recommendation: PLOS ONE issued an Expression of Concern about this article. The notice says Fig. 7 does not report data for an LSD1 siRNA experiment, so the result statement is not supported, while your Section 3 takes that knockdown result as its clearest indication that LSD1 drives migration. Hedge that Section 3 wording or replace it with independent evidence, and don't build new work on this result. The notice says similarities with other groups' work call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results, and your Background cites [12] for LSD1 being higher in lung cancer tissue. Hedge that sentence too and cite the notice next to [12].
